/staticQuestions/5/answer.source_en: Three signatures: bindae-tteok (mung-bean pancakes, the most famous Gwangjang dish and what the market is known for internationally — ≈₩5,000 per pancake, very filling); mayak gimbap (small bite-sized seaweed rice rolls in mustard-vinegar sauce, ≈₩3,000–₩4,000 per bundle, kid-friendly); and yukhoe (raw beef tartare in sesame oil, ≈₩15,000–₩20,000 — Gwangjang's yukhoe alley has multiple shops, the guide will recommend one). For non-adventurous eaters: kalguksu (knife-cut noodles, ≈₩7,000) or kimbap-and-tteokbokki sets are reliable.

/staticQuestions/6/answer.source_en: Residential. Most of the ≈900 hanoks in Bukchon are private homes; only some are tea houses, craft workshops, or small museums. The Red Zone tourist entry restriction applies 17:00–10:00 in the busiest residential area, but the city asks visitors to keep voices down at all hours. Don't enter private courtyards or photograph people without consent. The eight officially designated 'Bukchon Hanok 8 Views' are the photo-OK spots.
